entry.title: Windows 7 Desktop Widgets 1.0.0
entry.content:
Windows 7 Desktop Widgets

I really missed the classic Windows 7 desktop widgets and couldn't find a proper, lightweight version anywhere without bloat, broken scaling, or missing multi-monitor support. I love how simple and handy they were, so I made this accurate recreation. Enjoy!

What's included:

  • Classic Windows 7 Clock: All 8 original skins, second hand toggle, clock label, time zone picker, and the authentic desktop options window (click the wrench icon on the widget hover bar or right-click -> Options…).
  • Classic Windows 7 Calendar: Spiral-bound notebook with an expandable monthly grid (click the expand icon on the hover bar or double-click the calendar), date picking, and smooth navigation.
  • Clean & Fast: Each widget runs in its own lightweight window with native vector GDI+ rendering (no external images needed), per-monitor High-DPI scaling (125%/150%+), and full multi-monitor drag support.

☕ Support / Donations: If you enjoy this mod and want to support its author: Support on Boosty

entry.title: Rounded Selection Rectangle 1.0
entry.content:
English

Gives the rectangle you draw to select files rounded corners and a gentle fade when you release the mouse. Works on the desktop, in File Explorer and in apps that use standard Windows list controls.

  • Adjust the corner roundness, border width and background opacity.
  • Choose background and border colors independently, or keep Windows default for either one.
  • Set the fade-out duration, or use 0 to turn it off. The mod respects the Windows animation setting.

In Background color and Border color, choose Custom color and enter a color such as #8B5CF6. Windows default ignores the custom value and follows the system color. Custom colors affect only the selection rectangle.

Compatible with Win32 UI Modernizer.

Other selection-rectangle mods, such as Desktop Marquee Fade and Classic Selection Rectangle Color, can overlap with this mod's fade or override its colors. Disable overlapping features if you use them together.

This mod depends on symbols published by Microsoft. If a Windows update has no published symbols, or changes the symbols the mod uses, the mod will stop working until compatible symbols or an updated mod are available.

Rounded selection in Home (WinUI)

File Explorer's Home page uses WinUI. To round its selection rectangle, install and enable Windows 11 File Explorer Styler in Windhawk. In that mod's settings, add an entry under Control styles and set Target to:

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Shapes.Rectangle#SelectionRectangle

Under Styles, add each of these four lines as a separate style:

Fill:=<SolidColorBrush Color="{ThemeResource SystemAccentColor}" Opacity="0.25" />
Stroke:=<SolidColorBrush Color="{ThemeResource SystemAccentColor}" />
RadiusX:=8
RadiusY:=8

Save the settings. This uses the Windows accent color, a 25% opacity fill and 8-unit corner radii. To change the roundness, adjust both RadiusX and RadiusY. These styles are configured separately from this mod's settings.

Português

Deixa o retângulo que você arrasta para selecionar arquivos com cantos arredondados e um desaparecimento suave ao soltar o mouse. Funciona na área de trabalho, no Explorador de Arquivos e em aplicativos com listas padrão do Windows.

  • Ajuste o arredondamento dos cantos, a espessura da borda e a opacidade do fundo.
  • Escolha as cores do fundo e da borda separadamente, ou mantenha o Padrão do Windows em cada uma.
  • Defina a duração do desaparecimento, ou use 0 para desativá-lo. O mod respeita a configuração de animações do Windows.

Em Cor do fundo e Cor da borda, escolha Cor personalizada e informe uma cor como #8B5CF6. Padrão do Windows ignora o valor personalizado e acompanha a cor do sistema. As cores personalizadas afetam somente o retângulo de seleção.

Compatível com o Win32 UI Modernizer.

Outros mods de retângulo de seleção, como Desktop Marquee Fade e Classic Selection Rectangle Color, podem sobrepor o fade ou as cores deste mod. Desative as funções equivalentes se usar esses mods juntos.

Este mod depende dos símbolos publicados pela Microsoft. Se uma atualização do Windows não tiver símbolos publicados, ou alterar os símbolos usados pelo mod, ele deixará de funcionar até que símbolos compatíveis ou uma atualização do mod estejam disponíveis.

Seleção arredondada na pasta Início (WinUI)

A pasta Início do Explorador de Arquivos usa WinUI. Para arredondar seu retângulo de seleção, instale e ative o Windows 11 File Explorer Styler no Windhawk. Nas configurações desse mod, adicione uma entrada em Control styles (estilos dos controles) e preencha Target (alvo) com:

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Shapes.Rectangle#SelectionRectangle

Em Styles (estilos), adicione cada uma destas quatro linhas como um estilo separado:

Fill:=<SolidColorBrush Color="{ThemeResource SystemAccentColor}" Opacity="0.25" />
Stroke:=<SolidColorBrush Color="{ThemeResource SystemAccentColor}" />
RadiusX:=8
RadiusY:=8

Salve as configurações. Isso usa a cor de destaque do Windows, fundo com 25% de opacidade e cantos de 8 unidades. Para mudar o arredondamento, ajuste RadiusX e RadiusY. Esses estilos são configurados separadamente das opções deste mod.

Español

Da esquinas redondeadas y un desvanecimiento suave al rectángulo que arrastras para seleccionar archivos. Funciona en el escritorio, en el Explorador de archivos y en aplicaciones con listas estándar de Windows.

  • Ajusta las esquinas, el grosor del borde y la opacidad del fondo.
  • Elige los colores de fondo y borde por separado, o conserva el Predeterminado de Windows para cada uno.
  • Ajusta la duración del desvanecimiento, o usa 0 para desactivarlo. El mod respeta la configuración de animaciones de Windows.

En Color de fondo y Color del borde, selecciona Color personalizado e introduce un color como #8B5CF6. Predeterminado de Windows ignora el valor personalizado y sigue el color del sistema. Los colores personalizados afectan sólo al rectángulo de selección.

Compatible con Win32 UI Modernizer.

Otros mods del rectángulo de selección, como Desktop Marquee Fade y Classic Selection Rectangle Color, pueden superponer el desvanecimiento o los colores. Desactiva las funciones equivalentes si usas esos mods juntos.

Este mod depende de los símbolos publicados por Microsoft. Si una actualización de Windows no tiene símbolos publicados, o cambia los símbolos que usa el mod, dejará de funcionar hasta que haya símbolos compatibles o una actualización del mod.

Selección redondeada en Inicio (WinUI)

La página Inicio del Explorador de archivos usa WinUI. Para redondear su rectángulo de selección, instala y activa Windows 11 File Explorer Styler en Windhawk. En los ajustes de ese mod, añade una entrada en Control styles (estilos de controles) e introduce lo siguiente en Target (destino):

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Shapes.Rectangle#SelectionRectangle

En Styles (estilos), añade cada una de estas cuatro líneas como un estilo separado:

Fill:=<SolidColorBrush Color="{ThemeResource SystemAccentColor}" Opacity="0.25" />
Stroke:=<SolidColorBrush Color="{ThemeResource SystemAccentColor}" />
RadiusX:=8
RadiusY:=8

Guarda los ajustes. Esto usa el color de énfasis de Windows, un fondo con un 25% de opacidad y esquinas de 8 unidades. Para cambiar el redondeado, ajusta RadiusX y RadiusY. Estos estilos se configuran por separado de las opciones de este mod.

entry.title: Crazy Time 0.7.0
entry.content:
Crazy Time

A minimalist scheduler for shutdown, sleep and hibernate, living in the notification area. Português abaixo.

This mod really shuts down, sleeps or hibernates your computer when a schedule fires. Save your work first. A warning notification appears before the action, and you can cancel or postpone an occurrence from the panel.

Windows 10 is untested. It was developed and tested on Windows 11 only. It is expected to work on Windows 10 (version 1809 or newer for the dark theme of the controls), but this has not been verified. Please report issues.

What it does

  • Schedule an action by duration (1 minute to 7 days), at a date and time, or repeating on chosen weekdays.
  • Keep several schedules at once: edit, pause, cancel one occurrence, postpone it by 10 minutes, or delete.
  • Countdown warnings at 30, 15, 10, 5 and 1 minute, with optional sound.
  • Schedules at the same instant are detected and refused.
  • Optional per-schedule "force apps to close" (shutdown only), off by default, with a data-loss warning.
  • Actions the computer cannot perform are explained instead of scheduled.
  • Portuguese and English; automatic, light or dark theme; high contrast.

How to use

  1. Enable the mod. A tray icon appears; click it to open the panel.
  2. Pick the action and how it is scheduled, then press Add schedule.
  3. Click the tray icon to open the panel again. Closing the panel keeps the countdown running; right-click the icon or use Options to exit. Exit stops scheduling until Windhawk restarts or the mod is toggled off and on again; Windhawk still lists the mod as enabled.
  4. Disabling the mod stops everything and removes the icon. Schedules are saved per user; occurrences that expired while the mod was off are not run.

Schedules are stored in Windhawk's mod storage, in a file named with your user SID. On first use, an existing legacy LocalAppData schedule file is copied there without overwriting an existing destination. The legacy file is kept as a backup. Removing the mod deletes Windhawk's managed storage; the legacy backup remains.

Português

Agendador minimalista de desligar, suspender e hibernar, na área de notificação.

Este mod realmente desliga, suspende ou hiberna o computador quando um agendamento dispara. Salve seu trabalho antes. Uma notificação de aviso aparece antes da ação e você pode cancelar ou adiar a ocorrência pelo painel.

Não testado no Windows 10. Desenvolvido e testado apenas no Windows 11. Deve funcionar no Windows 10 (versão 1809 ou mais nova para o tema escuro dos controles), mas isso não foi verificado. Relate problemas.

Como usar: ative o mod, escolha a ação e o tipo de agendamento (por duração, data e hora, ou repetição semanal) e clique em Adicionar agendamento. Clique no ícone da barra para reabrir o painel; fechar o painel não interrompe a contagem. Desativar o mod encerra tudo. Sair interrompe os agendamentos até reiniciar o Windhawk ou desativar e reativar o mod; ele ainda aparece como ativado no Windhawk.

entry.title: Nested Tray Drawer 0.1.13
entry.content:
Nested Tray Drawer

Add a second drawer to Windows 11's hidden notification-icons panel. Drag an icon onto the added chevron to collect it, then click the chevron to open the second drawer. Both drawers can remain visible together. Icons retain their native templates, input handlers and app context menus. The footer is 40 DIP high.

Concept illustration; example icons and panel styling are illustrative.

Experimental compatibility

Runtime validated on Windows 11 23H2 build 22631.5126 x64 with Windhawk 1.7.3, Taskbar.View.dll 2125.4507.10.0 and taskbar.dll from that installation. ARM64 builds and offline identity/symbol checks are also provided, using ARM64 taskbar.dll 10.0.26100.9549, SystemTray.dll 2608.26001.100.0 and Taskbar.View.dll 2125.26100.0.0. ARM64 UI behavior has not been tested on a physical device and remains experimental. Windows 10, other Windows builds, DPI/monitor combinations and interactions with other tray mods are unverified.

The mod discovers SystemTray.dll, older Taskbar.View.dll or ExplorerExtensions.dll and resolves the required internal interfaces and methods from symbols. It no longer requires a particular DLL version, timestamp, image size or vtable address. This does not make every Windows build supported: the symbol names, root layout and native identity ABI must still be compatible.

Persistent identity uses Wh_Disasm to follow a recognized interface-adjustment thunk and the HWND/UID/GUID copy on x64 or ARM64. Both constructor-based and inlined identity getters are recognized; the native owning-string return type is never called across C++ ABIs. Unrecognized symbols, instructions, field layouts or call targets are rejected rather than guessed. Some older ARM64 binaries (such as the inspected taskbar.dll 10.0.22621.3810) lack the required Identity() symbol. Do not bypass these checks to force compatibility.

Use

  1. Open the normal taskbar hidden-icons drawer.
  2. Drag an icon onto the added chevron and release it. Repeat to collect more.
  3. Click the added chevron to open or close the second drawer. Both drawers can remain open; an empty second drawer does not open.
  4. Right-click the chevron and choose Restore all collected icons to return every collected icon and explicitly clear saved membership.

There is no right-click icon picker or individual drag-out command. Disabling the mod using Windhawk's own toggle restores the native tray and preserves the saved collection. There is no second enable setting.

Saved collection

Records use Windhawk's public storage API, with a Windows-user SID suffix to separate users in installed Windhawk. Membership uses an app GUID, or the owning process's exact executable path and native UID. Missing apps keep their records; ambiguous or inaccessible identities remain visible. Changed app identifiers can require recollection. Records contain app identifiers/encoded paths, not secrets; the encoding is not encryption. No records are transmitted.

An invalid record is kept intact and icons remain visible. The chevron's context menu offers Reset saved collection for explicit recovery; a readable invalid API record is backed up before resetting. Uninstalling removes Windhawk-owned storage. Updates and Explorer restarts preserve the collection within the same mod ID.

Known limits

  • Custom app menus that do not expose foreground native menu state can dismiss both drawers after the bounded menu-start grace period.
  • Complete Explorer restart, full mouse/keyboard and drag-cancel coverage, light/high-contrast appearance and live theme switching remain untested.
  • Symbol discovery across module families is implemented; runtime compatibility on 24H2/25H2 is not established by the local build tests.

Credits

Native overflow access is adapted from m417z's GPLv3 Taskbar notification icon spacing. Symbol-based interface resolution and vtable verification follow Ris Peng's GPLv3 System Tray Folders. The Wh_Disasm instruction-scanning approach follows m417z's GPLv3 Taskbar height and icon size. Nested Tray Drawer keeps a separate simultaneous flyout and drag-based membership; it does not replace the first drawer with an in-grid folder view. The single-file mod retains its GPL-3.0 declaration.

entry.title: Task View Customizer 1.0.0
entry.content:
Task View Customizer

Customize Windows 11 Task View's layout and appearance using its existing virtual desktop thumbnails and window overview. Choose where the desktop list appears or show it without the window overview. Customize background materials, theme colors, desktop highlights and the New desktop button. Control hover switching, slide direction and scrolling speed while keeping the native controls.

Task View modes

  • Windows default: keeps desktops at the bottom while applying the mod's layout and appearance settings. This is the default mode.
  • Full Task View with desktops at the top: moves the desktop list above the window overview.
  • No Task View with Desktop list in the top: shows only the desktop list near the top of the screen.
  • No Task View with Desktop list at the center: shows only the desktop list, centered on the screen.
  • No Task View with Desktop list at the bottom: shows only the desktop list near the bottom.

The mod does not change Alt+Tab or the desktop preview shown when hovering over the taskbar's Task View button.

Screenshots

| Full Task View with Desktops list at the top | Desktop list at the center + Fit desktop tiles | Windows default + Fit desktop tiles | | :---: | :---: | :---: | | | | |

Settings

Task View behavior

Choose the mode, hide the New desktop button, or close Task View in any mode when the Windows key is released. In list-only modes, Tab navigates desktops and clicking outside the list closes it. Key-release closing requires holding Windows while using the list, then releasing it.

Desktop list layout

Choose full width, fit the desktop tiles, or set a percentage of the screen. Adjust the frame margin. Taskbar clearance follows the taskbar's actual edge and size on each monitor, including small/default taskbars and display scaling. Space already excluded by Windows is not counted twice. Windows default mode keeps desktops at the bottom while applying these sizing controls. Enable Prevent switching desktops on hover to suppress delayed mouse-hover selection of desktop thumbnails. Click a desktop to switch instead. The option applies to all Task View modes and leaves keyboard navigation available. Desktop hover switching delay (ms) sets the wait before that preview switches. The default is 400 ms, matching the current Windows mouse-hover delay read by Task View. Enter 0–600000; blank or invalid text preserves the native delay. Prevent switching desktops on hover takes priority over this setting.

New desktop button

The button follows the last desktop by default. Enable Move New desktop button to the right to keep it at the list's right edge while desktops scroll. Width, stretch, background and plus-sign alignment controls apply in both positions. Adjust the button width, hide its background, or position the plus sign. Stretch New desktop button to highlight height extends the button to match its hover/selection frame and hides the New desktop label. The width and plus-sign alignment settings still apply. Turn the toggle off to restore the original vertical layout. Stretching also applies to Windows default mode through the shared button layout.

Background materials

Choose Native, Solid color, Acrylic, Clear, or experimental Mica. Solid starts opaque and can be made translucent without blur. Acrylic uses a live blurred backdrop and tint. Clear removes the material. You can also hide the list background in list-only modes or remove its outer border without removing desktop selection borders.

Material transparency accepts 0-100. Zero keeps the material's default strength; 100 makes Native, Solid and Acrylic backgrounds clear. Values outside that range use default strength; -1 is the default setting. Thumbnails and labels remain visible, and native hover/focus brush alpha is preserved rather than turning faint highlights opaque.

Mica uses a panel-local blurred wallpaper brush with color and luminosity blends. Its transparency control reduces tint/luminosity while keeping the wallpaper layer opaque. This is an experimental approximation of the native window material: its appearance can differ from apps using Windows' DWM Mica backdrop. It falls back to a solid color when unavailable. Windows can also use Acrylic's solid fallback when transparency is disabled. Hiding the desktop list background takes priority over material styling.

Desktop highlights

Keep Windows' highlight or choose border only, background only, or both. The highlight background opacity controls the hovered/selected desktop fill.

Theme colors

Set background and border colors independently for dark and light mode. Accepts native, accent, #RRGGBB, or #AARRGGBB. accent follows the current Windows accent color; invalid values preserve native colors. Background colors also provide Acrylic/Mica tint and custom highlight fill. Border colors apply to panel borders and custom highlights.

Full-screen backdrop

Keep the native backdrop, clear it, or use Acrylic with adjustable dimming. The list-only disable-blur option keeps the wallpaper clear even when Windows transparency is enabled. It is independent of the desktop strip's background. An explicit backdrop choice overrides the disable-blur option.

Animations and scrolling

Choose Desktop list animation direction: From the bottom (default) or From the top, independently of Task View mode. This controls entrance and exit motion. Disable Task View animations independently of the background material. Adjust desktop reveal scrolling speed from 10-500%: 100% uses Windows' current speed, 50% is half speed, and 200% is double speed.

Compatibility

Designed for Windows 11. Windows builds can change Task View's internal control names and layout; unrecognized controls are left alone. Mica remains experimental. Mixed-DPI monitors, desktop drag and drop, and interactions with other shell customization mods can depend on the Windows build.

No PDB debugging symbols or byte-pattern scanning are required. Desktop-slide direction uses public animation properties and live layout geometry; unrecognized or ambiguous slides are left unchanged.

entry.title: Brave Acrylic 3.9
entry.content:
Brave Acrylic

Very important — Symbol cache: Controlled and maintained by bardelyne, the author of Brave Acrylic. This is an author-hosted cache, not an official Windhawk service. Our GitHub Actions workflow checks for new Brave releases and prepares small compatibility files from Brave’s official symbols. Windhawk downloads the matching file for your installed Brave build and caches it locally. The large symbol files are processed by the workflow; your PC receives only the small compatibility data.

Reveal the Windows backdrop through Brave's vertical tab area, frame, toolbar, address field, and webpage area. Add rounded acrylic menus and native popups, plus blur behind address-bar suggestions. Native background targeting works across theme colors. Use a website-styling extension for backgrounds painted by websites.

Alpha software. Translucent Windows is required, configured for brave.exe. Brave Acrylic exposes the background; Translucent Windows supplies the effect.

Restart Brave after applying the mod, updating it, or changing its settings. Close all Brave windows normally and exit any remaining background Brave instance, then reopen it. This rebuilds native windows and their cached backgrounds.

Requirements

  • x64 version of Brave.
  • Windhawk with Brave Acrylic enabled.
  • Translucent Windows configured to apply a translucent effect to brave.exe.
  • Windows Transparency effects enabled.

Compatibility

Windows 11 is the tested environment. Windows 10 is unverified; the backdrop provider and selected effect must support that Windows version. Native ARM64 Brave is unsupported.

The native-popup suggestion method was tested with Brave 1.98.60 and with regular Brave 1.98.62 / Chromium 156, including YouTube with Zen Internet transparency enabled. The current native contract is validated separately against those two official DLL/PDB pairs. Other builds need valid compatibility data for their exact chrome.dll. Native interfaces and rendering behavior can change and may require a mod update.

The earlier background-only native contract was validated on seven official releases from Brave 1.93.138 through 1.98.62 (Chromium 151–156). This checks the native compatibility data; it is separate from visual testing. See the compiler study.

Fast setup

  1. Enable Translucent Windows for brave.exe and choose the desired backdrop.
  2. Enable Brave Acrylic. Leave Vertical tabs background, Toolbar, and Webpage background on.
  3. Close all Brave windows normally and reopen Brave. Exit its background instance too if it stays running.
  4. Optionally use Zen Internet or Stylus to remove backgrounds inside websites, as explained below. Stylus requires custom CSS.

No theme-color setup is required.

Controls

| Setting | Default | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | Vertical tabs background | On | Reveal the backdrop behind the vertical tab area and browser frame. | | Toolbar | On | Clear the toolbar, bookmarks bar, and unfocused address-field backgrounds. Focused address fields keep their native theme. | | Webpage background | On | Clear only Chromium's background behind the webpage area, including its default white fallback. Website HTML, CSS, and content are unchanged. Use Zen Internet or Stylus for website backgrounds; Stylus requires custom CSS. | | Acrylic menus | On | Blur native context menus, the main menu, and submenus. Text, icons, selection, and input stay native. | | Acrylic popups | On | Blur supported native browser bubbles and the native Extensions manager. Extension and website HTML overlays keep their own styling. | | Blur search suggestions | On | Use a native results popup with Windows blur below the input cutout. Typed text, result text and input remain native and sharp. | | Hide duplicate Windows buttons | Off | Optional workaround that removes the real Windows system-menu style. It can affect Alt+Space, taskbar menus and other window tools. Prefer Brave's Use compact mode option in Appearance. | | Use online symbol cache | On | Let Windhawk download small exact-build files from the author-controlled cache. Turn off to use existing local cached symbols only, then restart Brave. |

Restart Brave after applying settings, even when a change appears immediately. Some backing views and native popup choices are created with their windows. Webpage backing can apply on tab selection without refreshing the page; restarting after disabling it restores existing renderer defaults. The caption-button option can apply immediately.

Website backgrounds with extensions

Webpage background clears only Chromium's backing layer underneath websites, including the default white fallback. It does not modify website HTML, CSS, or content. To remove backgrounds painted by a website, use a styling extension such as Zen Internet or Stylus.

Zen Internet

For backgrounds inside websites, install Zen Internet from the Chrome Web Store. Open the extension, go to Advanced Settings, and turn Disable Transparency off under Global Feature Controls. Keep Webpage background enabled in Brave Acrylic. Open a new tab or reload an existing page to apply extension setting changes.

Zen Internet applies website-specific styles; coverage and results vary by site. Brave Acrylic removes the browser's backing and white fallback so CSS-transparent page areas can reveal the Windows backdrop. The extension handles website styling. Brave Acrylic does not inject JavaScript or CSS into pages.

The extension's store page cautions that ordinary Chromium does not support transparent pages. Brave Acrylic provides the native transparency path; an extension alone cannot provide the Windows effect. The extension's source and website styles are available separately.

Stylus

Stylus from the Chrome Web Store lets you create and manage custom CSS styles for individual websites. It does not remove website backgrounds out of the box. You must write or paste CSS rules that make the desired backgrounds transparent, or install a suitable existing userstyle. Complex websites may need rules for several background elements. Keep Webpage background enabled in Brave Acrylic so those transparent areas reveal the backdrop.

See the Stylus guide to writing styles for creating a style and limiting it to a particular website.

How it works

Brave's existing transparent-host path enables its compositor to preserve transparency. The mod removes the actual vertical-tab backing through Brave's own setter and clears selected native background roles within their paint clip. Child controls and text retain their original painting. Native focus checks preserve the focused address field.

The webpage option clears the native backing during content-view updates and sets Chromium's persistent page-base color when a tab is attached. That value is also used by future renderers, so switching or restoring tabs does not bring the default white background back. Explicit website backgrounds remain visible unless a website-styling extension changes them.

The full native path uses 29 functions, of which 20 are private hooks, and one immutable background-class vtable. Each feature has its own dependency set; unavailable features keep their native appearance. The implementation uses no sampled colors, private object-member offsets, guessed screen rectangles, screenshot polling, input forwarding, or GPU hooks. Normal DirectComposition stays enabled, with no special browser launch flag. Windows supplies the backdrop. Acrylic can turn gray when inactive; choose a suitable blur mode in Translucent Windows for the main window if you prefer a persistent effect.

Menus, popups and suggestions

Native menus and bubbles keep their own theme colors with reduced background alpha. A Windows host-backdrop visual sits underneath Chromium in the same popup window and follows its actual rounded background geometry. There are no extra overlay windows or input forwarding. A private composition worker owns its own dispatcher; disabling the mod closes its targets and joins that worker without changing Brave's dispatcher. If Windows cannot read the host-backdrop capability flag, cleanup removes the visual effect without guessing a prior flag value.

Tab and group hover cards, including their fading text and memory icons, keep their foreground painting. Their separate client and footer backgrounds are removed, while a tint derived from Brave’s own background color sits beneath Chromium’s content. This keeps the tint consistent during transitions and avoids black fade masks. The same native-popup path covers dialogs such as Restore pages?. Windows-drawn popup borders are suppressed where supported and their previous value is restored on unload.

The native Extensions manager also clears its repeated scroll-container backgrounds so they cannot cover the blur. Extension names, icons, pin buttons, menus and the Manage extensions button keep their native painting and input. This does not alter HTML content inside an extension's own popup.

Suggestions use Chromium's normal desktop-popup factory instead of its in-window Aura override. Windows supplies the blur behind that native results popup, which also works with the tested Zen Internet transparency setup. Chromium still owns its contents, layout, keyboard navigation and mouse input. Native view bounds and header height define a rounded window region below the address field; there is no input catcher or separate overlay. Resizing and DPI changes update the region, and cleanup restores the actual prior region on the owning UI thread. Restart Brave after applying this option so existing results widgets are rebuilt. These options do not turn website dialogs or extension HTML into acrylic. Windows high contrast and transparency preferences are cached and updated from Windows notifications off Brave’s paint path.

Symbol resolution, privacy and updates

Brave Acrylic resolves exact C++ prototypes and the background-class identity with Windhawk's supported HookSymbols / WH_HOOK_SYMBOLS_OPTIONS::onlineCacheUrl mechanism. Windhawk handles its ordinary local cache and optional online download. No build-specific addresses are embedded and remote PDB downloads remain disabled. The mod retains local executable-range, unwind-boundary, approved-leaf, thunk and overlap checks before registering hooks.

Small named-symbol files are published under brave-acrylic-features-v7/ on our symbol-cache branch. They contain the native function locations needed for each Brave build. The service and publishing workflow are controlled and maintained by bardelyne.

Windhawk handles compatibility downloads and local caching through its standard mechanism. Our workflow uses pinned actions and checks the official Brave archive and matching symbols before publishing. See cache hosting for the technical details.

No telemetry, uploads or login: the mod only downloads compatibility data through Windhawk. Browser cookies, history, page content, settings and account details stay on your PC. Turn Use online symbol cache off and restart Brave to use suitable existing local cached symbols only.

The workflow requests a check every two hours, with a backup 30 minutes later. GitHub can delay or drop scheduled starts, so this is not an exact timer. It checks the stable release, asset identities and native contract before downloading large files. Unchanged releases skip browser and PDB downloads. Both generation and publication use the run's same source revision; large official files stay on the GitHub runner. Restart Brave after newly required compatibility data becomes available.

The extractor handles verified compiler folding according to each function's role, while rejecting unrelated sharing on patched functions. The workflow reports compatibility separately for vertical tabs, the toolbar, webpage backing, menus, popups, and suggestions. A missing or changed function disables only its dependent features. Validated features are still published, and the workflow summary lists unavailable features with their reasons. Invalid files, mismatched symbols, failed downloads, and publishing errors still stop publication.

Duplicate corner buttons

If two sets of minimize/maximize/close buttons appear, first enable Use compact mode in Brave Settings → Appearance. The optional Hide duplicate Windows buttons workaround is off on a fresh install because it removes the window's actual WS_SYSMENU style. Windows system menus, taskbar interactions, accessibility tools or other window managers may be affected. Disabling the option or unloading the mod restores its recorded style changes.

Troubleshooting

Restart Brave after installing or applying changes: close all windows and its background instance, then reopen normally. Enable Windhawk debug logging to check each feature's availability or a symbol-cache message. For website styling, check Zen Internet's transparency setting and whether that site has a supported style, or check the CSS and site scope of your Stylus style.

Windows 8/8.1 Family Safety Applet Restorer

This mod restores the classic Windows 8/8.1 Family Safety (Parental Controls) Control Panel applet that was removed from modern versions of Windows.

IMPORTANT: svchost.exe must be included in the mod's target processes.

Screenshots

About

The mod downloads the original Windows binaries from Microsoft’s public symbol server on first use, verifies them with pinned SHA-256 hashes, applies the necessary compatibility patches in memory, and registers the applet virtually so that no permanent system files are modified.

It supports 6 languages: English, Italian, Persian, Spanish, French and Portuguese.
The language can follow the Windows UI language or be forced to a specific locale.

The applet appears under User Accounts in Control Panel Category view and can also be opened directly.

Note: it might take a minute to load the applet because the mod downloads the required dependencies.

entry.title: Taskbar Open Window Underline 2.0
entry.content:
Added

  • Icon underline (experimental) — a settings group that draws a line under each button's icon with the same open/minimized rule as the label underline, so the mod also works with "Combine taskbar buttons and hide labels".
  • A composition SpriteVisual attached to Image#Icon via ElementCompositionPreview::SetElementChildVisual, sized and positioned relative to the element (RelativeSizeAdjustment / RelativeOffsetAdjustment): it follows the icon through resizes and DPI changes with no layout code and never enters the taskbar's layout.
  • Options: thickness, width (% of the icon), distance from the icon (negative moves it over the icon), corner radius, opacity, color.
  • Color: #RRGGBB / #AARRGGBB; light|dark variants; comma-separated horizontal gradients; both combinable. Empty uses the system accent color. The theme is read from SystemUsesLightTheme, since the taskbar follows the system theme.
  • Corner radius: a CompositionGeometricClip with a rounded-rectangle geometry whose size is bound to the icon element's visual by an expression animation, so it tracks the line's relative width; 0 disables the clip.
  • Colors are cached and refreshed through UISettings::ColorValuesChanged, which covers accent changes and system theme switches; subscribed whenever the icon underline is on; the brush and clip are rebuilt only when their parameters change, identified by their Comment.
  • Visuals are tagged with a Comment, tracked only as weak element references, and hidden and detached when the option is turned off and on unload. An element that already carries another mod's child visual is left alone.
  • Hide the running indicator — hides the taskbar's own indicator under running buttons so the underline is the only cue. The same element marks the active window and, on some builds, attention requests, so those markers are hidden too (intended). Independent of the icon underline. Implemented by setting IsVisible(false) on Rectangle#RunningIndicator's hand-off composition visual rather than its XAML properties, which the button's visual states would overwrite; restored when the option is turned off and on unload, handing control back to XAML.

Changed

  • A button without a label is evaluated when the icon underline or the indicator option is on; the view-model resolver works from the ItemsRepeater item, not the text. The title fallback still requires a label.
  • README: icon-underline screenshot, the hidden-labels dependency on the view-model symbols, and the new options.

entry.content:
Quick Settings Media Progress Bar for Windows 11

Adds a modern, interactive seek bar and live playback timestamps directly to the default Windows 11 Quick Settings (Win + A) media player widget.

Features

  • Interactive Seeking & Scrubbing: Click or drag the progress bar thumb to seek smoothly within any playing track.
  • Mouse Wheel Scrubbing: Hover anywhere over the progress bar and scroll the mouse wheel to seek forward or backward.

  • Multi-Session Support: Seamlessly switches timeline and position when switching between active media apps using the Quick Settings arrows.
  • Zero XAML Diagnostics Conflicts: Uses direct COM-interface symbol hooks in ControlCenter.dll, completely avoiding XAML Diagnostics. Fully compatible with Windows 11 Taskbar Styler, Notification Center Styler, and File Explorer Styler.
  • Auto-Restoring: Cleanly restores the native media player card when the mod is disabled or unloaded.

entry.title: Cursor Idle Fade 1.1.0
entry.content:

Fixed

  • Remote desktop clients: the cursor could stay permanently invisible or never fade inside a remote desktop client such as RustDesk. These apps take their own copy of the system cursor. If the copy is made while the cursor is faded, the app keeps an invisible cursor. If it’s made while the cursor is visible, the app’s cursor never fades.

Behaviour details

Known limitation

  • The mod can’t update cursor copies that other apps have already made. Exclusion prevents the problem for the listed programs only. If another app shows the same behaviour, add its executable name to the list.

entry.title: Recycle Bin Tray 1.0.0
entry.content:
Recycle Bin Tray

A lightweight Windhawk Windows 11 mod that places an interactive Recycle Bin directly into your system tray.

The icon follows the current Recycle Bin state, can optionally disappear when the bin is empty, reacts to Windows Shell notifications, and supports multiple rendering styles, themes, and configurable mouse actions.

The mod is designed to remain lightweight and self-contained while integrating with the native Windows Shell wherever possible.

Features

⚠️ Drag & Drop is disabled by default. Enable Enable drag & drop in the mod settings to use this feature.

  • Drag & Drop to Recycle Bin — drag files and folders directly from the Desktop, File Explorer, or other applications that expose dropped files through the standard Windows CF_HDROP format. Deletion follows the Windows Recycle Bin policy for each source drive. If the icon is in the ^ notification-area overflow menu, open the menu and drop directly onto the Recycle Bin icon.
  • Live Recycle Bin state — updates when items are added to or removed from the Recycle Bin.
  • Four icon styles:
  • system — use the native Windows Recycle Bin icon.
  • vector — render a lightweight custom vector Windows 11-style icon.
  • font — render a glyph from an installed font family.
  • custom — load an .ico, .png, .bmp, or .jpg file.
  • Three vector variants — choose between a minimal geometric style with a lifted-lid full state, a Fluent-inspired trapezoidal style, and a compact symbolic style.
  • Separate icons for states and themes — custom mode uses Empty/Full Light-theme files with optional Empty/Full Dark-theme alternatives.
  • Optional auto-hide — automatically hides the tray icon while the Recycle Bin is empty.
  • Light / dark theme support — vector and font rendering adapt to the current Windows system theme; custom icons use Light-theme source files, optional Dark-theme alternatives, and can automatically adapt transparent monochrome image colors to the active theme.
  • Automatic recovery — a configurable fallback timer periodically checks the Recycle Bin state in case a Shell notification is missed.
  • Taskbar restart recovery — the tray icon is recreated after Explorer or the Windows taskbar is restarted.
  • DPI-aware rendering — the render target follows the tray's DPI, while Shell-reported tray geometry is tracked separately for layout changes. Vector icons are rendered at high internal resolution for smoother results.
  • Configurable mouse actions — independently configure left click, double-click, middle click, and right click.
  • Recycle Bin context menu — open, empty, or open Properties using Windows Shell-provided localized labels when available.
  • Optional empty confirmation — keep or disable the confirmation dialog before emptying the Recycle Bin.

Installation

From Windhawk

  1. Open Windhawk.
  2. Go to the Explore tab and search for Recycle Bin Tray.
  3. Click Details, then click Install.
  4. Open the mod's settings to customize the icon and mouse actions.

Manual Installation from Source

  1. Install and open Windhawk.
  2. Click Create Mod.
  3. Copy the mod source code and paste it over the template code.
  4. Click Compile Mod and enable the mod.

The mod runs as a dedicated Windhawk tool mod rather than being injected into explorer.exe, isolating it from the Windows Shell (see Mods as tools).

No separate installation, executable, or Windows service is required. Windhawk manages the process automatically.

Using the Tray Icon

The tray icon provides configurable actions for each supported mouse input.

Mouse actions

| Input | Available actions | | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | | Left click | Open, context menu, empty, Properties, do nothing | | Double-click | Open, empty, Properties, do nothing | | Middle click | Empty, open, context menu, Properties, do nothing | | Right click | Context menu, open, empty, Properties, do nothing |

Each action can be configured independently from the Windhawk settings.

Click / double-click behavior

Windows sends a single-click notification before it can determine whether a second click will arrive.

When a double-click action is enabled, the mod therefore waits for the Windows double-click interval before executing the single-click action.

This small delay is intentional. Removing it while keeping independent single- and double-click actions could cause a physical double-click to execute the configured single-click action as well.

Single-click execution is deferred by the Windows double-click interval so that a physical double-click executes only its configured double-click action. If Double click action = Do nothing, a physical double-click therefore performs no action.

Drag & Drop

Drag & Drop is disabled by default. Enable Enable drag & drop in the mod settings before using this feature. When enabled, the feature uses a global low-level mouse hook (WH_MOUSE_LL) to detect the start of drag gestures.

The Recycle Bin tray icon can then be used as a normal drag & drop destination for files and folders.

Simply drag one or more items from:

  • the Windows Desktop;
  • File Explorer;
  • other applications that expose file lists through the standard Windows CF_HDROP format;

and drop them directly onto the Recycle Bin tray icon.

The mod receives the dropped items through the standard Windows OLE drag & drop mechanism and asks the Windows Shell to process them according to the Recycle Bin policy configured for each source drive.

Deletion policy and safety

Drag & drop follows the per-drive Recycle Bin policy configured in Windows for each dropped item.

If a drive is configured to remove files immediately instead of moving them to the Recycle Bin, items dropped from that drive can be permanently deleted. The Windows delete-confirmation preference is respected.

If Windows cannot recycle a selection, for example because it exceeds the configured Recycle Bin capacity, the Shell may display its native warning or confirmation before allowing permanent deletion. Cancelling that prompt leaves the operation uncompleted.

Visibility and overflow menu

For drag & drop to remain available, Hide when empty must be turned off so the Recycle Bin icon continues to exist as a target.

Windows may place the icon in the ^ notification-area overflow menu when it first appears.

Keeping it visible is recommended for quicker access.

The icon does not need to stay permanently visible in the main system tray.

  • If it is visible directly in the tray, drop files and folders onto it normally.
  • If it is in the ^ overflow menu, open the menu and drop files and folders directly onto the Recycle Bin icon.

If you want to keep the icon permanently visible, move it out of the overflow menu:

  • Manual placement: Drag the icon out of the overflow menu and place it directly in the main system tray area. Windows will remember this placement.
  • Windows Settings (if available): Go to Settings → Personalization → Taskbar → Other system tray icons and toggle the icon to On.
  • Windhawk alternative: On modern Windows 11 builds where native toggles may be missing or restricted, you can use the Always show all taskbar tray icons mod to keep all icons permanently visible.

Desktop focus behavior

Windows Explorer may occasionally fail to initiate a drag from a Desktop file when another application currently has focus.

For example, clicking a Desktop file and immediately moving the mouse may be interpreted primarily as a focus or selection operation instead of starting the drag.

This happens before the drag operation reaches the mod and is related to normal Explorer Desktop behavior.

Workarounds

Two simple workarounds are available:

Option 1 — focus the Desktop first

Click the file once without dragging, then start the drag operation again.

Option 2 — hold the mouse button briefly

Press and hold the left mouse button for approximately 500 ms before moving the file.

Once Explorer has successfully initiated the drag operation, dropping the item onto the Recycle Bin works normally.

The mod does not synthesize or force a Desktop drag when Explorer has not started an OLE drag operation. A low-level mouse hook is used only to arm the tray drop overlay; the actual data transfer still requires the source application to start normal OLE drag & drop.

Context Menu

The optional Recycle Bin context menu contains:

  • Open
  • Empty Recycle Bin — disabled when the bin is already empty
  • Properties

Menu labels are loaded from localized shell32.dll resources when available, so they follow the current Windows display language. The popup itself uses native Win32 menu rendering without custom menu icons.

English fallback strings are used when a corresponding Shell resource cannot be loaded.

Emptying the Recycle Bin

The Confirm before emptying option controls confirmation for actions that empty the Recycle Bin through the mod, independently of the Windows Display delete confirmation dialog option in Recycle Bin Properties.

When enabled, the standard Windows confirmation dialog is shown before the Recycle Bin is emptied.

When disabled, the mod requests the silent empty operation directly.

For emptying actions triggered through the mod, this setting takes precedence over the Windows Recycle Bin confirmation preference.

Icon Styles

Choose one icon style: System · Vector · Font · Custom Icon

System

Uses the Windows Shell's own Recycle Bin icon.

This is the simplest option and generally provides the closest match to the native Windows appearance.

Vector

The icon is generated at runtime with GDI+ instead of loading an image file.

It is designed for a clean Windows 11-style appearance and is rendered at a 4× internal resolution before being reduced to the final tray size for smoother edges.

Three variants are available:

  • Style 1 — minimal geometric 24×24 silhouette. The empty state uses a closed lid; the full state lifts the lid and exposes two compact content shapes while keeping the body unchanged.
  • Style 2 — Fluent-inspired trapezoidal body optimized for tray-size rendering. The empty state uses a clean outline, while the full state uses the same silhouette with a filled body.
  • Style 3 — compact symbolic silhouette with a simple lid, handle, and body. The empty state uses an outlined body, while the full state uses the same silhouette with a filled body.

Font

The icon is drawn from glyphs provided by installed font families.

The empty and full states have separate font family / typeface, glyph, and font weight settings. Font and glyph fields are intentionally blank by default: if Font mode is selected without a usable configuration, the mod falls back to the native Windows Recycle Bin icon.

Font names are matched against GDI font/typeface names exposed by Windows. Leading/trailing whitespace and surrounding quotation marks are ignored when settings are loaded. GDI limits the requested typeface name to 31 characters (LF_FACESIZE - 1); longer names are rejected instead of being silently truncated.

The Font weight option is available independently for the Empty and Full states and supports the standard Windows range from Thin (100) to Black (900). Use the base family/typeface name with the desired weight when Windows exposes the family through normal weight matching. If Windows exposes a variant as a separate typeface (for example Font Awesome 7 Free Solid or Arial Narrow), enter that exact Windows typeface name instead. When an exact weight is unavailable, Windows can select the nearest available weight in the requested family.

Fallback behavior

Font mode validates both the requested font family and glyph before rendering:

  • Empty state: if the empty-state font or glyph is unavailable, the full-bin font/glyph configuration is used automatically.
  • Full state: if the full-bin font or glyph is unavailable, the native Windows Recycle Bin icon is used.
  • If the empty state falls back to the full configuration and that configuration is also unavailable, the native Windows Recycle Bin icon is used.

This lets a font with only one suitable trash/delete glyph remain usable without showing a missing-glyph square.

Entering a glyph code

Glyph values can be entered as hexadecimal Unicode code points with or without the 0x prefix.

Examples:

0xF014
F014

To find a code point, you can use:

  • Windows Character Map (charmap.exe) to inspect installed fonts.
  • The documentation/reference of the font you are using.
  • Microsoft's references for Segoe Fluent Icons or Segoe MDL2 Assets when using those font families.

Recommended fonts & glyphs

| Font Family | State / role | Glyph Code | Notes | | --------------------------------- | ------------ | ---------- | ----- | | Font Awesome 7 Free | Empty | 0xF014 | Recommended example for the empty state. | | Font Awesome 7 Free Solid | Full | 0xF014 | Recommended example for the full state. | | Segoe Fluent Icons (Built-in, default Windows 11 icon font) | Single state | 0xE74D | Delete; no distinct empty/full Recycle Bin pair. Best used with Hide when empty enabled. | | Segoe MDL2 Assets (Built-in, legacy Windows icon font) | Single state | 0xE74D | Delete; no distinct empty/full Recycle Bin pair. Best used with Hide when empty enabled. | | Material-Design-Iconic-Font | Full | 0xF154 | Optional third-party example. |

The two built-in Segoe icon fonts are useful when a single Delete symbol is sufficient. Because they don't provide distinct empty and full Recycle Bin states, they work best with Hide when empty enabled and the Delete glyph configured for the full state: the tray icon is then hidden while the Recycle Bin is empty and shown when it contains items. If you want an always-visible icon with visually distinct empty and full states, another font is preferable.

Custom Icon

Custom mode accepts:

  • .ico
  • .png
  • .bmp
  • .jpg

Images are automatically resized to match the current system tray icon target size.

For the cleanest raster result, use artwork designed to remain readable at small tray sizes. Ideally, use a source close to the active tray target size or a clean integer multiple of it (for example 16×16, 32×32, 48×48, or 64×64 when appropriate). Avoid oversized raster artwork with hairline details: a stroke that looks clean in the source can become sub-pixel when Windows renders the tray at 16 px (100% scaling), where no resampling method can fully reconstruct the original visual weight. The actual tray target depends on the Windows display scale factor; refer to the Theme and DPI Handling table below.

Custom Icon color handling can either preserve the colors stored in the selected source image or Automatically adapt monochrome image colors to the active theme. Theme adaptation reads the selected image's alpha channel, downsamples it by exact pixel-area coverage, and recolors the resulting mask in memory for the active Light or Dark theme. At the smallest 16 px Dark-theme target, a small stroke-preservation and coverage adjustment helps thin monochrome artwork retain more visual weight. For best results, still use simple transparent monochrome artwork designed to remain readable at small sizes; very fine raster details can remain softer at 100% display scaling. No source file is modified. Native .ico files and images without an alpha channel keep their original colors.

For transparent monochrome images, the Light theme Empty and Full files are normally enough. If a Dark-theme field is blank, the corresponding Light-theme file is reused automatically. The optional Dark theme section is only needed when you want different source artwork in Dark theme.

| If you want… | Use | | --- | --- | | Keep the icon's original colors | Keep original image colors | | Automatically match a transparent monochrome icon to the Light/Dark theme | Automatically adapt monochrome image colors to theme | | Use different artwork in Dark theme | Configure the optional Dark theme image |

Looking for ready-made icons? Icons8 is a useful resource for finding icons suitable for custom .ico / .png files.

For .ico files, a multi-size icon containing a 16×16 px layer is recommended for a crisp tray result.

You can paste a Windows path copied with Copy as path directly into the setting, including the quotation marks added by Windows. The mod automatically removes surrounding quotes and unnecessary whitespace.

Examples:

[Light theme → Empty bin] "C:\Users\YourUsername\Pictures\recycle_empty.png"
[Light theme → Full bin]  D:\CustomIcons\recycle_full.png
[Dark theme → Full bin]   D:\CustomIcons\recycle_full_dark.ico

Local paths are strongly recommended for optimal performance and to avoid delays if a network share is unavailable or goes to sleep.

Custom mode uses two Light-theme source files plus optional Dark-theme alternatives:

| Recycle Bin state | Light-theme file | Optional Dark-theme file | | ----------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------ | | Empty | customIcon.light.empty | customIcon.dark.empty | | Full | customIcon.light.full | customIcon.dark.full |

The Light-theme file is always selected in Light theme. In Dark theme, the matching Dark-theme file is selected when configured; otherwise the Light-theme file is reused automatically. When Automatically adapt monochrome image colors to the active theme is selected, the selected transparent monochrome image is recolored in memory for the current theme.

When a custom file cannot be loaded, the mod automatically falls back to the Windows system Recycle Bin icon.

Recycle Bin State Detection

The mod uses Windows Shell APIs to query the current Recycle Bin state and register for Shell notifications.

The current state and tray icon are initialized immediately. The first Shell notification subscription is established after a short Explorer/taskbar stabilization window and uses Windows' SHCNRF_NewDelivery delivery mode.

Shell notifications allow the icon to react quickly when items are added to or removed from the Recycle Bin. A configurable fallback timer periodically checks the actual state in case a notification is missed.

The default fallback interval is 300 seconds and can be changed in the Windhawk settings. DPI and tray-geometry changes are handled through Windows display/DPI events and the Shell-reported tray rectangle. Bounded startup retries handle cases where the Shell or tray is not yet ready.

Theme and DPI Handling

The tray icon is regenerated when Windows reports a relevant theme or display configuration change.

The mod derives its icon render target from the tray/display DPI.

| Scale Factor | Icon Size | | ------------ | --------- | | 100% | 16×16 px | | 125% | 20×20 px | | 150% | 24×24 px | | 200% | 32×32 px | | 250% | 40×40 px | | 300% | 48×48 px | | 400% | 64×64 px |

The target size is obtained from the current tray/display DPI. The rectangle returned by Shell_NotifyIconGetRect is tracked separately as a geometry-change signal; its slot bounds are not treated as a documented HICON target size.

Vector icons are rendered internally at 4× the target resolution before being downsampled with high-quality interpolation to fit the active tray size. This reduces jagged edges while keeping rendering and memory usage low.

Taskbar / Explorer Restart Recovery

The mod listens for the standard TaskbarCreated message.

When Windows Explorer or the taskbar is restarted, the mod recreates the tray icon automatically.

This allows the icon to recover without requiring the Windhawk mod to be manually restarted.

Technical Notes

  • The tray icon is hosted by a hidden top-level tool window owned by the mod's dedicated tray thread.
  • Drag & drop uses the standard Windows OLE IDropTarget mechanism and accepts dropped file lists exposed through CF_HDROP.
  • Dropped items are processed asynchronously on a dedicated STA worker through IFileOperation, so Shell UI or slow storage does not block the source application's DoDragDrop call. The worker is created lazily on the first accepted drop.
  • A passive IFileOperationProgressSink tracks operation results and logs failures without changing the Shell operation.
  • The mod does not create a separate executable or Windows service.
  • GDI+ is initialized lazily only when vector rendering or custom raster-image loading requires it; native .ico loading can bypass GDI+. Once initialized, it stays available for the lifetime of the tool and is released during final teardown.
  • Tray timers are explicitly cancelled during window destruction before icon and Shell resources are released.
  • Explorer/taskbar restarts are detected through the standard TaskbarCreated broadcast received by the hidden tray host.
  • The current icon handle is explicitly destroyed whenever the icon is replaced or the mod unloads.
  • The tray thread uses Per-Monitor V2 DPI awareness, follows the rectangle reported by Shell_NotifyIconGetRect, and tracks slot geometry changes independently from the DPI-derived render size.
  • A transparent top-level helper window provides the physical per-monitor DPI reference and is also used as the OLE drop overlay when drag & drop is enabled.
  • Explorer owns notification-area placement. If Windows exposes the tray on multiple taskbars, drag & drop follows the single icon rectangle returned by the Shell API.
  • A low-level mouse hook runs on a dedicated message-pump thread only while drag & drop support is enabled to detect the beginning and end of a potential drag; OLE IDropTarget remains responsible for the actual drop.

Settings Reference

The Windhawk settings are grouped by function:

  • General — visibility and icon style.
  • Vector — vector variant selection.
  • Font — font family and glyph values for empty/full states.
  • Custom Icon — color handling, Light-theme Empty/Full source files, and optional Dark-theme files.
  • Actions — mouse-button behavior and empty confirmation.
  • System — fallback Recycle Bin state refresh interval.

Renderer-specific settings only apply to the corresponding selected icon style.

For example, the Vector section is used only when Icon style is set to Vector.

Troubleshooting

The icon does not appear

Check that the Recycle Bin is not empty if auto-hide is enabled.

If the icon is still missing:

  1. Disable and re-enable the mod in Windhawk.
  2. Try restarting Windhawk.
  3. Check whether Windows has moved the icon into the notification-area overflow menu (^).

Windows may place the icon in the overflow menu when it first appears. This is normal. If you want it permanently visible, drag it from the overflow menu into the main system tray area; Windows will remember the placement.

Drag & Drop does not work

  1. Check the mod's settings to ensure that Drag & Drop is enabled and Hide when empty is turned off.
  2. If the icon is in the ^ overflow menu, open the overflow panel and drop onto the Recycle Bin icon itself.
  3. Make sure the source application provides dropped files through the standard Windows CF_HDROP format.

If dragging from the Desktop does not work, check whether another application currently has the input focus.

In that situation, either:

  • click the Desktop/file once before starting the drag; or
  • hold the left mouse button for approximately 500 ms before moving the file.

The dark theme does not apply

Check your Windows personalization settings to ensure that global dark mode is active.

For custom icons:

  • with Original colors, add an optional Dark-theme file if you want different artwork or colors in Dark theme;
  • with Automatically adapt monochrome image colors to the active theme, use a transparent monochrome image with an alpha channel. Native .ico files and images without an alpha channel keep their original colors.

Custom icons do not display

Verify that:

  • the configured path is correct;
  • the file exists and is accessible;
  • the image format is supported;
  • the selected Color handling mode matches the type of image you are using.

For raster images, choose a source size appropriate for the current display scale using the Theme and DPI Handling table; thin diagonal strokes can retain some aliasing at very small tray sizes. For .ico files, a multi-size icon containing a 16×16 px image is recommended.

If a custom icon cannot be loaded, the mod automatically falls back to the Windows system Recycle Bin icon.

A font glyph does not display

Check that:

  • the configured Font name exactly matches the Windows GDI font/typeface name;
  • the Glyph value is a valid Unicode hexadecimal code point (for example 0xF014);
  • the selected font actually contains a glyph at that hexadecimal code point.

If either the font name or glyph code is incorrect or unavailable, Font mode falls back according to the rules described in the Font section above.

entry.title: Middle-Click New Tab Chrome/Edge/Brave 1.1
entry.content:
• Added support for vertical tabs in Edge and Brave: middle-clicking the empty area below the tabs opens a new tab.

  • In Edge, the empty area is detected with UI Automation. It can be turned off with the new Edge vertical tabs setting.

  • Renamed the mod title and description to make it clear that it's for browsers.
